text: {"question":"How do the CMB and large‑scale structure data sets described in Passage A influence the redshift evolution of the total equation‑of‑state parameter shown in Passage B for the ΛCDM, SGPAge, and TGPAge‑Fix models?","reference_answer":"The high‑ℓ Planck, ACT, and SPT‑3G likelihoods, together with the low‑ℓ Planck and CMB‑lensing measurements, tightly constrain the early‑time behaviour of the models, keeping wtot close to 1/6 near matter–radiation equality. The inclusion of the low‑ℓ EE and SROLL2 EE data, as well as the combined ACT+Planck lensing likelihood, further restricts the late‑time evolution, driving wtot toward −1 at z≈0 for all three models.","passage_1_contribution":"Passage A lists the specific CMB and lensing likelihoods (Planck PR4 CamSpec, low‑ℓplik, SROLL2 EE, ACT DR6, SPT‑3G D1, and their lensing variants) that provide the observational constraints used in the analysis.","passage_2_contribution":"Passage B presents the redshift dependence of wtot, wX, and the density parameters for the ΛCDM, SGPAge, and TGPAge‑Fix models, illustrating how these quantities evolve across cosmic history.","joint_reason":"The question requires understanding how the observational data sets (Passage A) shape the theoretical predictions for wtot shown in Passage B, linking the empirical constraints to the model‑dependent evolution curves.","same_quantity":false}
